topic: How does defocused feed array placement optimize coverage versus scan loss in DBF architectures?
consensus_response: Defocused feed array placement optimizes coverage versus scan loss by manipulating the array factor's spatial filtering properties. Non-uniform spacing between elements reduces grating lobes and increases tolerance to element failures, minimizing the impact of failed elements on overall system performance. This design approach enables more flexible beamforming and reduced sidelobes, particularly in point-to-point communications adopting MIMO principles.
reference_context: The defocused feed array placement has a significant impact on average unit cell loss, decreasing from 8.46 dB (2 dB scan loss) to 0.17 dB (2 dB scan loss), as reported in [1].
